regulated.q: Under HIPAA, what must be in place before an LLM vendor may receive a hospital's PHI?
options: A SOC 2 Type I report from the vendor
A signed Business Associate Agreement covering that service
A DPIA approved by an EU regulator
An ISO 27001 certificate covering the hospital
regulated.why: Vendors handling PHI for a covered entity must sign a BAA first. SOC 2 and ISO reports are helpful evidence but do not replace it.

regulated.q: What does PCI DSS scope reduction through tokenisation achieve?
options: It encrypts card data so every system can store it safely
It removes the need for any payment provider audits
Systems that see only tokens stay out of the cardholder data environment
It lets you keep card security codes after authorisation
regulated.why: If your system receives only a token and never the real card number, it is not part of the cardholder data environment. Security codes must never be stored after authorisation.

regulated.q: A federal agency asks for your AI search tool. Which question matters most early?
options: Which FedRAMP baseline they need and whether each service is authorised in that region
Whether their staff prefer a chat window or a search box
Which programming language their team knows best
Whether they have a SOC 2 report of their own
regulated.why: Federal agencies can only use authorised cloud services, and a model or store missing from the government region can decide the whole architecture.

regulated.q: A German insurer wants personal data kept in the EU. Which part of an AI build is most often forgotten?
options: The main database region
The web server region
The user interface language
Prompt logs, vector indexes and the model endpoint
regulated.why: Teams usually place the database correctly but forget copies in logs, observability tools, vector stores, eval sets and the model provider's endpoint.

regulated.q: Spot the mistake: 'We are compliant, so the bank's security review is a formality.'
options: Security reviews are only needed for healthcare customers
Banks accept any SOC 2 report, so the claim is fine
It names no framework, version or scope, and reviews take weeks
Compliance only matters after the pilot is in production
regulated.why: A claim of compliance must say which framework, version and scope it covers, and bank security and model risk reviews take real time, so they should start early.

fieldlife.q: What is usually the slowest part of your first week at a new customer?
options: Writing the first working prototype
Getting access: VPN, accounts, data roles and devices
Choosing a programming language
Booking travel for the next month
fieldlife.why: Access requests often need several approvals, so submit them on day one with a named approver each and follow up.

fieldlife.q: What is cognitive empathy in customer work?
options: Understanding someone's view and incentives without having to agree
Sharing the customer's emotions so they feel supported
Agreeing with stakeholders to avoid conflict
Reading body language to detect when people lie
fieldlife.why: Cognitive empathy is understanding how someone sees a situation and what drives them, which helps you find what would make a blocker comfortable.

fieldlife.q: A manager asks you to 'also quickly' build a letter generator during your pilot. What do you do first?
options: Build it that evening so the relationship stays good
Refuse because it is not in the statement of work
Write it down, size it and give the sponsor trade options
Ask the manager to raise a ticket with your support team
fieldlife.why: Writing, sizing and trading keeps the decision with the sponsor and protects the agreed goal without a flat refusal.

fieldlife.q: You support three accounts and keep losing time switching between them. What helps most?
options: Answer every message within ten minutes
Drop the smallest account without telling anyone
Work on all three every hour to keep them equal
Block time by account and keep a current-state note for each
fieldlife.why: Longer blocks per account and a short state note at the top of each account's file reduce the reload cost of every switch.

fieldlife.q: Spot the trap: 'The customer has my mobile number, so they can reach me any time.'
options: It creates a personal on-call line that leads to burnout
Customers should never know an FDE's name
It breaks data residency rules
Mobile numbers are only allowed for executive sponsors
fieldlife.why: Support should run through agreed hours and a team escalation path, not one person's phone, or peaks turn into a permanent state.

interviewrounds.q: What does a recruiter screen mostly filter for?
options: Algorithm speed on hard problems
Deep system design knowledge
Interest, basic fit, communication and practical details
The quality of your open-source contributions
interviewrounds.why: The recruiter checks fit, clarity and logistics such as location, travel and salary; technical depth comes in later rounds.

interviewrounds.q: In a debugging round, what should you do right after skimming the README and layout?
options: Rewrite the module you think is messy
Reproduce the failure and read the full error and trace
Guess the fix and submit quickly
Ask the interviewer where the bug is
interviewrounds.why: Reproducing and reading the full trace gives you evidence for your first hypothesis; a visible method scores well.

interviewrounds.q: The design prompt names a hospital using Okta SSO and an old document store. How do you open?
options: Draw the standard RAG architecture straight away
Pick a vector database and justify it
Estimate queries per second before anything else
Ask about users, data, permissions, residency and the old store's access
interviewrounds.why: FDE design rounds score whether you gather the customer's constraints first, because they shape the whole design.

interviewrounds.q: A take-home has a 4-hour limit and you run out of time. What is the best move?
options: List what you cut and why in the README
Keep working for two more days to finish every feature
Submit without a README so they read the code
Skip the tests to add one more feature
interviewrounds.why: Reviewers usually open the README first, and a clear note on trade-offs and cuts shows judgement and respect for the limit.

interviewrounds.q: Spot the mistake in this STAR answer: three minutes on context, 'we' throughout, no result.
options: STAR answers should skip the situation entirely
Too long on setup, unclear personal role, and no measured result
Behavioral answers should always be under 30 seconds
Using a failure story is never acceptable
interviewrounds.why: Keep the situation short, say what you did with 'I', and end with a number or clear outcome.

portfolio.q: How many repositories can you pin to the top of a GitHub profile?
options: Three
Ten
Up to six
As many as you like
portfolio.why: GitHub lets you pin up to six repositories; pin your three or four strongest.

portfolio.q: What should a reviewer see in the first screen of a project README?
options: The full list of dependencies
The problem, a demo image, the headline result and quick setup
A history of every version
The licence text
portfolio.why: Most reviewers decide from the first screen, so lead with what it does, proof it works and a number.

portfolio.q: You want to show a claims tool you built at work. What is the safest approach?
options: Publish the code with the company name removed
Share screenshots of the internal tool only
Put the repo on GitHub as private and share the link
Rebuild the pattern with synthetic data and label it a sample scenario
portfolio.why: Employer code, data and screenshots need written permission; a clean rebuild with synthetic data shows the skill without leaking anything.

portfolio.q: Your recorded demo is 11 minutes, mostly setup and code. What should you change first?
options: Script it to about 3 minutes around the user, problem, tool and result
Speed the video up to double speed
Add background music to keep attention
Split it into eleven one-minute videos
portfolio.why: Short scripted demos that start with the user's problem get watched; setup and code detail can live in the README.

portfolio.q: Spot the trap: a profile with 40 pinned-looking tutorial repos and 'Skills: Python, RAG, AWS'.
options: Tutorial repos are fine as long as they are public
Listing skills is enough proof for FDE roles
Strong work is buried and nothing proves the claimed skills
The profile needs more repos to look active
portfolio.why: Reviewers spend seconds; a few featured projects with results prove skills that a list only claims.
